WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bunny’s Growing Garden Worksheet for Age 4

Bunny’s garden day in three pictures — write 1, 2 and 3 to put planting, watering and blooming in order.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Sequencing a three-step story is the first true comprehension skill: your child decides what happens first, next and last from pictures alone. Numbering the boxes turns that thinking into marks on paper, and the draw panel invites the ending no one can predict — what Bunny plants next.

  • Sequencing a 3-step story
  • First / next / last language
  • Number writing
  • Predicting what comes next

On the sheet: Write 1, 2, and 3 to put the story in order!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Teddy’s Missing Backpack Worksheet for Age 4

Teddy’s backpack is missing! Follow the room’s clues and circle the card where the backpack waits.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Using picture clues to answer a where question is early inference: the scene shows the backpack on the hook, and the cards test whether your child can match clue to answer. Ask “how do you know?” — the pointing and explaining is the comprehension muscle.

  • Reading picture clues
  • Matching a clue to an answer
  • Explaining a decision
  • Playroom vocabulary

On the sheet: Look at the clues. Circle where Teddy should look!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Lion’s Feelings Worksheet for Age 4

A gift, a dropped ice cream, a popped balloon — draw lines from each story to the feeling it gives Little Lion.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Matching events to emotions teaches the heart of story comprehension: characters feel things for reasons. Your child connects each mini-story to its feeling face, then the draw panel asks for a feeling of their own — which is where the real conversations start.

  • Matching events to feelings
  • Emotion vocabulary (happy, sad, surprised)
  • Line drawing between cards
  • Talking about feelings

On the sheet: Match each story to the correct feeling!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Rainy Day Surprise Worksheet for Age 4

It was sunny, then the rain came — circle what Fox will do next with the umbrella he found.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Predicting what happens next is the comprehension move strong readers make automatically. The story pictures carry the whole proof: sunny first, rainy second, and a blue umbrella left on the bench. Ask your child to POINT at the clue before circling — the pointing is the thinking.

  • Predicting what happens next
  • Using picture clues
  • Matching weather to actions
  • Explaining an answer

On the sheet: Circle what will happen next!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Owl’s Storybook World Worksheet for Age 4

A goldfish, a farmer, an astronaut — match each character to the place where their story happens.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Characters belong to settings: matching each one to where its story happens builds the who-and-where questions every reading comprehension lesson starts with. The places are pictured, not written, so pre-readers play on equal footing.

  • Matching characters to settings
  • Story vocabulary (ocean, farm, space)
  • Line drawing
  • Answering where questions

On the sheet: Match each character to where the story happens!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Puppy’s Helping Hands Worksheet for Age 4

Three problems, six puppy choices — circle the best way for Puppy to help in each row.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Choosing the helpful action (and noticing the unhelpful one) is problem-and-solution thinking. Because every correct answer here is a KIND one, the sheet doubles as a kindness chat: ask why the other choice wouldn’t help, and let the draw panel sketch a way your child helped this week.

  • Problem and solution matching
  • Evaluating two choices
  • Kindness vocabulary
  • Explaining a decision

On the sheet: Circle the best way to help!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Squirrel’s Mixed-Up Morning Worksheet for Age 4

Wake up, brush, breakfast, off to school — write 1, 2, 3 and 4 to un-mix Squirrel’s morning.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A four-step routine sequence stretches the first-next-then-last chain one step further than most four-year-olds need to track — which is exactly the right stretch. Mornings are also the routine your child knows best, so the order can be checked against real life.

  • Sequencing a 4-step routine
  • Number writing 1–4
  • Time-of-day words
  • Comparing to your own morning

On the sheet: Write 1, 2, 3, and 4. to put the story in order!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Giraffe’s Picture Detective Worksheet for Age 4

Two balloons, a blue kite, a rabbit on the swing — look hard at the playground and circle the right answers.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This is the classic look-and-answer format: three questions whose answers hide in one busy scene. Counting balloons, naming a color and identifying a character each practice a different detail skill, and every answer must be pointed at in the picture first.

  • Counting objects in a scene
  • Naming colors
  • Identifying characters
  • Answering from a picture

On the sheet: Look carefully. Circle the correct answers!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Duckling’s Cause & Effect Worksheet for Age 4

A drooping flower, a muddy puddle, a sailing boat — draw lines matching what happened to why it happened.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Cause and effect is the question readers ask forever: WHY did that happen? Pairing each what with its why (sun, rain, wind) trains the habit early, with pictures instead of print. The draw panel flips it round: your child draws a what, and YOU guess the why.

  • Cause and effect matching
  • Weather vocabulary
  • Line drawing between columns
  • Asking why

On the sheet: Match what happened to why it happened!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Hedgehog’s Story Map Worksheet for Age 4

Every story has a WHO, a WHERE and a WHAT — circle all three for Hedgehog’s apple-tree story.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A story map is the first graphic organizer readers meet, and this sheet is the gentlest version: one question per row, three pictured choices each. Completing it gives your child the whole skeleton of a story — character, setting, event — which they can then retell aloud.

  • Identifying character, setting, event
  • Story map vocabulary
  • One answer per question
  • Retelling from a map

On the sheet: Find WHO, WHERE, and WHAT happened!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Mouse’s Story Retelling Train Worksheet for Age 4

Mix the batter, bake the cookies, munch one — match each picture to the BEGINNING, MIDDLE or END train car.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Beginning-middle-end is the retelling frame used all through school, and the train makes it physical: three cars, three pictures, one story. The baking story is deliciously checkable too — nobody eats a cookie before it’s baked!

  • Beginning / middle / end structure
  • Sequencing by logic
  • Retelling a process
  • Number order 1–3

On the sheet: Match each picture to BEGINNING, MIDDLE, or END!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Bear’s Big Decision Worksheet for Age 4

A crying friend, a busy road, a spilled cup — circle the best thing for Little Bear to do next.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Each row gives a small dilemma and two actions: one kind or safe, one careless. Choosing and JUSTIFYING (out loud!) is decision-making practice wrapped in a story. The road row is worth an extra beat — crossing with a grown-up is a real-life rule worth rehearsing.

  • Best-choice reasoning
  • Safety rules (roads, spills)
  • Kindness decisions
  • Explaining a choice

On the sheet: Circle the best thing to do next!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Beaver’s Story Bridge Worksheet for Age 4

Gather the logs, build the bridge, cross the river — circle what happened FIRST and what happened LAST.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Picking out just the first and last beats of a three-part story is a focused sequencing workout: the middle must be ignored on purpose, which is harder than it sounds. Engineering-minded children will happily retell every bolt of the bridge afterwards.

  • First and last in a story
  • Ignoring the middle on purpose
  • Retelling a build story
  • Picture comparison

On the sheet: Circle what happened FIRST and LAST!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Rabbit’s Hidden Clues Worksheet for Age 4

Snowy, rainy, hungry — read Rabbit’s clues in each row and circle the thing Rabbit needs.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Needs-based clues are inference with stakes a four-year-old understands: cold means coat, rain means umbrella, hungry tummy means sandwich. The two wrong items per row are pleasantly silly, which invites the best comprehension move of all — explaining WHY not.

  • Matching needs to situations
  • Clue reading
  • Explaining why not
  • Weather and food vocabulary

On the sheet: Look at the clues. Circle what Rabbit needs!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Penguin’s Silly Story Fix Worksheet for Age 4

A sneaker getting brushed, a bicycle in a nest — one picture makes sense, one is silly. Circle the one that fits!

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Silly-versus-sensible is a comprehension game children beg to replay: the silly picture breaks the story, and spotting the break proves the child has a working model of how the world goes. Every fix deserves a giggle and a “why is that silly?”

  • Does-it-make-sense reasoning
  • Story logic repair
  • Explaining silly choices
  • Real-world common sense

On the sheet: Circle the picture that makes sense!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Butterfly’s Story Journey Worksheet for Age 4

Garden to pond to forest to flower field to sunny meadow — follow Butterfly’s journey and skip the silly stops.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A journey story gives sequencing a map: five stops in order, three indoor impostors to refuse. The dotted route on the sheet can be traced with a finger first, then numbered — and the bedroom/kitchen/snowy mountain refusals are where the reasoning giggles live.

  • Sequencing a 5-stop journey
  • Rejecting wrong places
  • Order words (first, then, next, last)
  • Habitat common sense

On the sheet: Draw a line to follow Butterfly’s journey!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Raccoon’s Memory Challenge Worksheet for Age 4

A red blanket, two apples, a blue cup — look hard at Raccoon’s picnic, cover it, then circle what you remember.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Memory-for-pictures is the quiet skill under every comprehension test: hold a scene in your head, then answer about it. The fun move is covering the scene (a spare sheet of paper works) between questions — the answers must come from memory, not eyes.

  • Visual memory for details
  • Counting from memory
  • Color naming
  • Answering without looking

On the sheet: Look at the story. Circle what you remember!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dragon’s Story Ending Studio Worksheet for Age 4

A planted seed, a baking day, a bike ride — circle the ending that truly fits each Dragon story.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Predicting endings is the comprehension move strong readers make automatically, and this sheet rehearses it three times: seeds bloom (not bicycles), flour bakes (snowmen need not apply), and helmets mean riding. Each wrong ending is a lovely “why not?” conversation.

  • Predicting story endings
  • Cause-and-effect endings
  • Rejecting silly endings
  • Story vocabulary

On the sheet: Circle the ending that fits the story!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Turtle’s Story Timeline Worksheet for Age 4

Pack the basket, picnic, wash the dishes — circle what happened BEFORE the picnic and what happens AFTER.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Before-and-after questions build timeline thinking: the picnic is the middle, and everything else must be sorted around it. (Printed-art quirk, fixed in play: the best after-the-picnic answer — washing the dishes — sits in the Before row of the art, so on paper the grown-up key below is the referee.)

  • Before and after reasoning
  • Timeline thinking
  • Daily-routine logic
  • Story-order words

On the sheet: Circle what happened BEFORE and AFTER!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Koala’s Character Detective Worksheet for Age 4

A gardener, a baker, a mail carrier — draw lines matching each character to the job they did in the story.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Matching characters to actions is the who-did-what question at the heart of story comprehension, and jobs make it concrete: the whisk means baker, the watering can means gardener. The draw panel invites the best follow-up — which job would YOUR child pick?

  • Matching characters to actions
  • Job and tool vocabulary
  • Line drawing
  • Talking about work people do

On the sheet: Match each character to what they did!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Elephant’s Story Surprise Worksheet for Age 4

A party hat, three candles, a gift from Monkey — look at Elephant’s surprise and circle the correct answers.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Three story questions about one celebration scene: color, count and character. The party context makes every answer worth retelling, and counting candles is counting with a purpose — birthday ages are the numbers four-year-olds care about most.

  • Answering story questions
  • Counting candles (3)
  • Color identification
  • Who-did-what reasoning

On the sheet: Look at the story. Circle the correct answers!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Panda’s Picture Story Puzzle Worksheet for Age 4

Find the box, build the kite, hold it high, fly it — write 1, 2, 3 and 4 to order Panda’s kite day.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A four-step build-and-fly sequence with a delicious trap: flying LOOKS like it should come first because it’s the most exciting picture. Working out that the box of parts starts the story is exactly the logical ordering practice this class is for.

  • Sequencing a 4-step build
  • Resisting the exciting-first trap
  • Number writing
  • Making-and-doing vocabulary

On the sheet: Write 1, 2, 3, and 4 to put the story in order!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Otter’s Story Treasure Hunt Worksheet for Age 4

A blue bucket, two ducks, a red boat — follow Otter’s river clues and circle each treasure.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Clue-hunting on a riverbank scene: color, count and floating-object questions whose answers all sit in one busy picture. River vocabulary (bridge, reeds, rowing boat) gets a workout alongside the comprehension, and every answer can be pointed at first.

  • Answering clue questions
  • Counting ducks (2)
  • Color naming
  • River vocabulary

On the sheet: Look at the story. Circle the correct clues!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Ladybug’s Missing Story Scene Worksheet for Age 4

Seed, mystery middle, sunflower — circle the picture that completes Ladybug’s story.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Finding the MISSING middle of a story is sequencing turned detective: two anchors are given, and the middle must be deduced. Watering the sprout is the only choice that makes the seed become a sunflower — and the toy airplane and snowman are memorably wrong.

  • Filling a missing story beat
  • Growth sequencing
  • Rejecting silly middles
  • Garden vocabulary

On the sheet: Circle the picture that belongs in the middle!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dolphin’s Story Questions Worksheet for Age 4

A big splash in the ocean — find WHO jumped, WHERE it happened, and WHAT Dolphin did.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The classic who-where-what trio on one ocean scene: each question has three pictured answers, and the scene proves every one. Ocean vocabulary (wave, turtle, coral) rides along, and the draw panel invites the child’s own ocean story.

  • Who / where / what questions
  • Ocean vocabulary
  • Answering from a scene
  • Story retelling

On the sheet: Find WHO, WHERE, and WHAT happened!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Fox’s Story Shadow Mystery Worksheet for Age 4

Muddy footprints, an empty cookie plate, a tipped flowerpot — circle what happened in each of Detective Fox’s mysteries.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Reading clues to name what happened is inference with pictures: each clue rules out one suspect and backs another. The explaining is the growth point — “the footprints are muddy, so it was the puppy!” — and each wrong answer is a lovely chance to ask WHY not.

  • Reading picture clues
  • Inference (who did it?)
  • Explaining why not
  • Mystery vocabulary

On the sheet: Look at the clues. Circle what happened!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Squirrel’s Story Connections Worksheet for Age 4

A thirsty rabbit, a fallen nest, a wobbly wheel — draw lines matching each problem to its fix.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Problem-to-solution matching is empathy plus engineering: each left card needs help, and the right column holds exactly the fixes. Talking through WHY each fix fits (and why the others don’t) is the grown-up’s best move on this sheet.

  • Problem and solution matching
  • Helping vocabulary
  • Line drawing
  • Reasoning about fixes

On the sheet: Draw lines to match each problem with its solution!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Deer’s Story Paths Worksheet for Age 4

Rain at the window — choose the story path: watch the rain, take the umbrella, open it, and out for a walk.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A choose-the-path story: at each fork one choice keeps the rainy day sensible and one flies off to the beach or the snow. Because each choice changes the story, the sheet begs to be played twice — once sensible, once deliberately silly, with a retelling of both.

  • Story-path choosing
  • Keeping a story sensible
  • Weather reasoning
  • Retelling a chosen path

On the sheet: Follow the pictures in the right story order!

WORKSHEET · CLASS 29 · AGES 4 YEARS

Storybook Castle Challenge Worksheet for Age 4

Three story challenges guard the castle: order the planting, read the feeling, choose what happens next.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The grand finale mixes three comprehension skills on one sheet: sequencing (what happens FIRST), feelings (a gift brings happy) and prediction (umbrellas open before walks). Earning all three is a genuine badge moment — the castle picture on the sheet is the trophy shelf.

  • Mixed story skills (order, feelings, prediction)
  • Sequencing plant growth
  • Emotion reading
  • Prediction reasoning

On the sheet: Complete the three story challenges!
